disposition_reason: ITAL master's thesis (Burgon 2023, defended 28 Apr 2023). Chapter 2 reports Cd and Pb (and non-detects for As and Hg) in 23 Brazilian cocoa-bean samples and in 65 bean-to-bar plus 6 conventional chocolates, by cocoa-solids class and bean-origin region (Tabelas 2-4). Chapter 3 (ochratoxin A) is out of scope. Cu, Co and Se results are not tracked analytes.
disposition_locator: Ch.2 §2.1 (printed p.66), Tabela 1 (p.71), Tabela 2 (p.73), Tabela 3 (p.75), Tabela 4 (p.78), §3.4 (p.81)

study.design: market survey (bean-to-bar chocolates from e-commerce; conventional chocolates from local retail) plus commercial bean survey (master's dissertation, Ch.2)
study.material_scope: fermented and dried cocoa beans (n=23); bean-to-bar chocolates white/milk/semi-sweet/dark (n=65); conventional chocolates (n=6)
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Beans grown in Brazil: Amazonas (Borba, Manicoré, Nova Olinda), Bahia (Arataca, Ibirapitanga, Itabuna, Itajuípe, Porto Seguro), Pará (Novo Repartimento, Mocajuba), Espírito Santo (Linhares). Bean-to-bar chocolates bought from Brazilian e-commerce, grouped by stated bean origin; 6 conventional chocolates bought in Campinas-SP local market (bean origin not stated).
study.collection_period: cocoa beans collected 2020-2022; chocolate purchase dates not separately reported
study.sampling_unit: one bean lot sample or one retail chocolate product
study.method: Microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion; beans by ICP OES (As, Cd, Cu, Pb); chocolates by ICP-MS iCAP RQ with KED (75As, 111Cd, 202Hg, 208Pb, plus Co, Cu, Se)
study.lod_loq: Chocolate (ICP-MS): As LOD 0.015/LOQ 0.022; Cd 0.001/0.002; Pb 0.005/0.007; Hg 0.007/0.010 mg/kg. Beans (ICP OES): As 0.171/0.272; Cd 0.021/0.033; Pb 0.057/0.091 mg/kg (Tabela 1). Hg not analysed in beans.
study.basis: as received / as sold (ground beans; grated chocolate); no moisture or fat-free correction
study.qa: Chocolate: ERM BD512 Dark Chocolate Cd 90 ± 3%; NIST 1547 Pb 101 ± 1%; TORT-3 As 102 ± 1%, Hg 84 ± 10%. Beans: TORT-2 As 88 ± 2%, Cd 94 ± 2%, Pb 98 ± 14%. CV 2-14% (n=7).

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary labels the Cd exposure estimates (5.91 / 23.6 µg/kg bw) as 'per day'; the thesis computes them from monthly consumption (479.16 g/month) against the monthly PTMI, i.e. per month.

Stored summary reports Co intake as 0.5 / 1.97 mg/kg bw as in the thesis; arithmetic (1.88 mg/kg x 15.75 g / 60 kg) gives ~0.49 µg/kg bw/day, so the thesis unit is off by x1000 (Co is not a tracked analyte).
Stored summary takes bean LODs from Tabela 1 (Cd 0.021) without noting Tabela 4 footnote lists Cd LOD 0.171 (the As LOD) and censors Cd as '<0,17'.
Stored summary classifies milk chocolate as 40-50% cocoa (Ch.3 OTA classification); Ch.2 metals classification is 30-50%.
Stored summary says 'Amazonas cocoa beans 8/8 above 0.30'; consistent with table, but thesis conclusion says six Amazonia samples exceeded; summary does not flag this.

Primary analysed Hg only in chocolates (ICP-MS); the bean ICP OES method covered As, Cd, Cu and Pb only, although the abstract says As and Hg were not detected 'in any of the analysed samples'. Stored summary repeats the across-beans-and-chocolates wording.
Stored summary does not flag the internal conflict over the Brazilian IN 160/2022 Cd limit for >40% cocoa chocolate (0.40 in Ch.2 vs 0.30 in Ch.1).
unresolved: Region sample counts for bean-to-bar chocolates disagree: §2.1 lists AP 2, AM 9, ES 8, BA 38, RO 1, Mata Atlântica 4, PA 4 (=66); Tabela 3 lists AM 7, AP 2, BA 35, ES 8, Floresta Amazônica 2, Mata Atlântica 4, PA 5, RO 2 (=65); Tabela 6 (OTA subset) differs again. Region-level n cannot be verified.
Bean Cd censoring threshold (<0.17, apparently the As LOD) vs Tabela 1 Cd LOD 0.021 mg/kg: true censored values unknown; Bahia Cd mean 0.056 below the printed threshold.
Bean Pb: Tabela 4 max 0.313 mg/kg (Bahia) vs text 0.06-0.15; Bahia min '<0,001' below LOD; overall mean 0.010 below LOD. Which is correct cannot be determined.
Pará bean Cd: table '<0,17' vs text mean 0.060 mg/kg.
Treatment of non-detects in all means is not described.
Whether beans were analysed whole (with shell) or as nibs is not stated.
Chocolate purchase dates not reported; bean collection 2020-2022.
No per-sample table; Figura 11 bar chart not digitized.
Brazilian IN 160/2022 Cd limit for chocolate >40% cocoa cited as 0.40 (Ch.2) and 0.30 (Ch.1); not verified against the instrument here.
